Benefits Halcyon (Ember 8 at 9.9). Paired with the S2 no-automatic-sales-prohibition concession that benefits Northwind.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the appropriate regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a complete incident report within 10 business days. Reporting obligations apply even when the cause is not yet established.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A model with a failure rate above 5% must be reported to the regulator and placed under a regulator-approved, time-bound corrective-action plan, including retesting and any interim safeguards the regulator determines necessary. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale; the regulator may restrict or suspend sales if needed to address an unacceptable risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. For units already installed, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent safe mitigation plan; the completion deadline must be at least six years after this standard takes effect

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard is adopted.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: If a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, using regulator-validated incident and installation data, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and conduct a regulator-supervised risk assessment. The regulator must require a time-bound corrective-action plan and may require a recall when the assessment finds that a recall is necessary to address an unacceptable risk, including where corrective actions cannot adequately mitigate the hazard.

document.section_notes: S2 ends with no sales stop above 5% and no public per-model publication, while customers still receive per-model results, which protects the flagship Hearth 10 from a ban. S5 makes recall discretionary: the 8/100k figure now triggers only a regulator-supervised assessment, so the Ember 8 at 9.9 is not automatically recalled. S3 sets a six-year retrofit deadline, which favours Northwind given its 38% shut-off coverage. S1's 24-hour reporting applies to all thermal incidents while the cause is still unknown, which is strong for a sector where both firms had unreported incidents.
